pageCache.pageTitle: School Values | Manor Fields Primary School
pageCache.text:
Manor Fields Primary School
Manor Fields Primary School
Inspiring Learning for Life
Every child known.Every child included.Every child challenged to achieve.
Our Mission
At Manor Fields, we open doors through learning. We want every child to discover what they are capable of, find their voice and see possibilities for their future.
We combine high expectations with care, building strong foundations in knowledge and giving children opportunities to explore, create and achieve. We help them take pride in who they are, work through challenges and recognise the difference they can make to others.
Together with our families and community, we nurture a sense of belonging that gives children the confidence to step into the wider world—with curiosity, kindness and ambition.
Our Values in Action
At Manor Fields, our values shape how we learn, how we treat one another and how we care for our community. Children experience them through everyday moments: having the courage to ask a question, welcoming a new friend or trying again when something feels difficult. Working together with families, we help children understand these values and make them their own.
🌟 Aspiration
We encourage children to see what is possible.
We hold high ambitions for every child and help them take the steps towards achieving them. In lessons, children build on what they know, tackle new challenges and take pride in their progress. Books, visits and encounters with the wider world introduce possibilities they may never have imagined. We want every child to discover their strengths and feel excited about their future.
🤝 Community
We belong, we contribute and we care.
Every child and family is an important part of Manor Fields. We build relationships through listening, working together and celebrating one another’s achievements. Children contribute through pupil voice, school council and shared responsibilities. Links with local organisations, care homes and community events help them experience the difference their kindness and involvement can make.
🦁 Confidence
We help children find their voice and believe in themselves.
Confidence grows when children feel secure enough to have a go. Through classroom discussion, daily oracy and opportunities to share their learning, children practise expressing ideas and listening to others. Adults offer encouragement and support so that pupils can ask for help, learn from mistakes and gradually do more for themselves. We celebrate the quiet achievements as warmly as the ones everyone can see.
⚖️ Equality
Every child matters, and everyone deserves opportunities to flourish.
We value each child’s identity, experiences and contribution. Our teaching responds to different needs, giving children the support and challenge they require to participate and succeed. Through books, discussions and everyday interactions, pupils encounter different perspectives and learn to challenge unfairness. We help them understand that fairness can mean providing different support so everyone has the opportunity to thrive.
💛 Kindness
We notice others and choose to act with care.
Kindness lives in the small things: inviting someone to join a game, offering help or noticing when a friend is upset. Adults model respectful relationships and help children understand how their words and actions affect others. When difficulties arise, we support pupils to listen, reflect and put things right. We want children to know that asking for kindness and support matters too.
🌱 Resilience
We learn that challenges can be worked through, with support.
Children develop resilience through manageable challenges and encouragement. We help them recognise what is difficult, try useful strategies and learn from feedback. They practise starting again, improving their work and taking the next step. Asking for help is part of this process: we want every child to know that they can persevere without having to manage everything alone.

Manor Fields Primary School
Manor Fields Primary School
About Us
Welcome to Manor Fields Primary School
A very warm welcome to Manor Fields, where children and families are at the heart of our school.
We want every child who walks through our doors to feel known, valued and excited about what lies ahead. Childhood is a precious time, and we want our children’s days to be filled with discovery, friendship and the pride of achieving something they once thought they couldn’t.
Our vision, “Inspiring Learning for Life,” begins with knowing each child: their interests, their strengths, what makes them smile and where they need a helping hand. We listen to their ideas, celebrate their individuality and help them find their voice. We want them to know that their contribution matters here.
We are ambitious for every child. Through rich learning experiences, thoughtful teaching and encouragement, we help children build secure knowledge and the confidence to use it. We nurture curiosity, make room for creativity and support children to persevere through challenges. Every child deserves opportunities to discover what they love and see how far they can go.
Families are central to this journey. You know your children best, and we value the understanding you bring. We want you to feel welcome, listened to and comfortable talking with us, whether you are sharing a proud moment, asking a question or seeking support. Together, we can help your child feel secure, grow in confidence and flourish.
Our values of Aspiration, Community, Confidence, Equality, Kindness and Resilience shape everyday life at Manor Fields: the welcome at the gate, the encouragement in a lesson and the care children show one another. Our connections with Salisbury and the wider community offer further opportunities to explore, contribute and belong.
Above all, we want children to look back on their time here with happy memories, lasting friendships and a belief in themselves that stays with them. We hope this website gives you a glimpse of life at Manor Fields, and we would love to welcome you in person.
Jess ClarkeHeadteacher

Manor Fields Primary School
Manor Fields Primary School
Barnaby's Breakfast Club
Welcome to our web page...
What is Barnaby's Breakfast Club?
It is a club ( open to all children who attend Manor Fields from Reception to Year 6) that provides breakfast and activities before the school day starts.
Who work's at the club?
Barnaby's breakfast club is staffed by :
Miss D Berlie - Breakfast Club manager/Higher Level Teaching assistant
Mrs J Davis - Teaching assistant
Mrs N Romano - Teaching assistant
Mrs J Lawton - Teaching assistant
Mr G Browning - Tecahing assistant (cover)
What time can children arrive?
We are open from 7.50am (during term time only) and children leave us at 8.45am to go to their classrooms.
What happens at the club?
Children eat breakfast in the school cooking room and then take part in activities in the hall.
When can my child/children attend?
Once they are registered, by completing the registration forms which are available in the foyer, please pre- book your children in for the days you need prior to attending by text on 07762597827.
How much does it cost and how do I pay?
Sessions cost £3.50. Fees can be paid in cash or bank transfer. We are also currently registered with Edenred and Sodexo to accept their vouchers.
Who can I contact if I have any questions?
You can call Miss Berlie (manager) in person or by phone on 07762 597827 or leave a message at the school office.

Manor Fields Primary School
Manor Fields Primary School
Wraparound Care in partnership with PH ActiveEd
We are pleased to offer a high-quality After-School Club at Manor Fields Primary in partnership with PH ActiveEd. Our After-School Club gives children a safe, welcoming space to unwind at the end of the school day, with a light snack and a great balance of activities. There is time for outdoor play to burn off energy with friends, alongside more relaxed options such as Lego, games and arts and crafts, so children can choose how to spend their time and finish the day feeling happy.
Every session is fully organised and delivered by PH ActiveEd's own staff, using their own resources, so there is nothing for families to arrange beyond booking a place.
Safe, registered and trusted
PH ActiveEd is an Ofsted-registered childcare provider. All staff hold an enhanced DBS, paediatric first aid and safeguarding training as a minimum, and each setting has its own risk assessment in place.
Because PH ActiveEd is Ofsted registered, you can pay using Tax-Free Childcare and childcare vouchers, as well as by card.
Times, prices and full details
Please see the flyer below for session times, prices and what is included.
Bookings for September are made through PH ActiveEd's new online booking system. To register and book a place, visit:
https://bookings.phactiveed.co.uk/
This is a new booking page, so if you have not used it before you will need to re-register, even if you had an account previously. When you register, please follow all the on-screen instructions. Once registered, you can log back in at any time to make bookings.
For more information on childcare vouchers, Tax-Free Childcare, FAQs and policies, please visit https://phactiveed.co.uk/ and go to the For Parents tab.

Manor Fields Primary School
Governors
Welcome to the governor section of our school website. In this section you will find a list of our current governors and information detailing their roles, responsibilities and length of office.
We are very proud to have a committed team of governors at Manor Fields; all of whom are volunteers with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. Governors are appointed for a term of four years and are expected to attend meetings, participate in training and visit the school throughout the year.
Our Governing Body consists of representatives from our parents and carers, the community, the staff and the Local Authority. We also have an independent Clerk who is responsible for taking the minutes of our meetings and oversees our administration. We have 4 Full Governing Body meetings a year, in addition to meetings of the Finance and Premises Committee and Curriculum and Staffing Committee. The minutes of meetings of the Governing Body are available for perusal and can be obtained from the Head Teacher upon request.
Governors are responsible for making sure the school actively provides the best possible and highest quality education for its pupils and actively fulfils its role in the local community.
The Head Teacher is responsible for the day-to-day management of the school and the governors, in co-operation with the Head Teacher, set the school’s vision, alongside the strategies and policies, that will ensure our success in achieving it. We both challenge and support the school, acting as a critical friend by monitoring and evaluating the progress the school is making towards achieving its aims and objectives.
The Governing Body has a duty to monitor and approve the school budget and ensure that resources are appropriately balanced. We monitor attendance levels and evaluate how well groups of pupils are performing and ensure that we have a robust framework in place to enable our children to be safe.
Being a school governor can be demanding but is also an extremely rewarding role. Achieving the best outcomes for all our children is at the heart of all that we do.
If you wish to contact the governors you can do so by email at governors@manorfields.wilts.sch.uk.
Chair of Governors, Manor Fields Primary School

School Governors, September 2026
Maria is a Parent Governor and joined in 2017. She is a parent with a daughter at Manor Fields, currently aged 9. Maria has worked in the Public Sector for 20 years supporting vulnerable people, previous to this, she worked in a number of charitable organisations. Her present role involves managing the performance of a collection of community services, ensuring quality and improvement. This experience in public administration and community work is helpful in the governing role. Maria joined the Governing Body to make a positive contribution to the work of the school with a significant amount of work going on behind the scenes.
Vice Chair of Governors
I was appointed as a Governor in June 2019. It was clear very quickly that Manor Fields is a friendly, lively, hard working and happy place though I had a lot to learn!
Using my work experience effectively in a school setting was new to me but I have had lots of help from other Board members, from School staff and from good Governor trainings sessions.
Before retirement I worked for many years in care and protection services for people of all ages and had some special responsibilities for safeguarding children and vulnerable adults. Developing care and support services for children and families, both in England and elsewhere were also a big part of my work.
It is a real privilege for me to be a Governor at Manor Fields and to be entrusted with a lead role in Safeguarding and Attendance. Keeping children safe and encouraging the best possible learning opportunities for them are tasks I am very pleased I can contribute to. I share them with everyone at Manor Fields and with the children, families and carers who are all part of the School community .
Clerk to the Governors
Parent/carer Governors
I applied to join the governing body of Manor Fields as a Parent Governor during the Summer of 2026. I have a son who enrolled in the school in September 2025 and he is absolutely thriving, so I am I keen to help the school in any way that I can and to give something back. My husband and I knew Manor Fields was the school we wanted for our son as soon as we walked in. The welcoming environment and happy nature of the whole school community made us feel that our son would be happy and safe here as well as championed for his achievements and help him reach his potential.
I have a background in finance and a love of learning and hope I can be of service to the school. I am keen to champion inclusion of all our children at Manor Fields and make learning and the school environment accessible to all, whatever level of needs they have. I bring with me an understanding of some of the complex needs that children may have and hope that my experience can be of benefit to the governing body and in turn, the school.
Mrs Catherine Sharpe
It is such a privilege to be on the board of Governors of such a happy and caring school where the whole school community works tirelessly to provide a safe, secure and exciting learning experience for all its children. I come to the role from an educational background, having worked in early years and primary education for 37 years. Through my role I hope to support the staff as they continue to provide excellence in education and continue to build strong relationships between parents, carers and the school. I realise the importance of good governance and effective leadership and that this will have a positive impact on the children and staff at our school. Volunteering as a school governor is a wonderful and unique opportunity, and I feel privileged to make a contribution to the future of so many talented children.
I began my career as a teacher of English in the secondary school sector in Kent. I then worked in Alternatives to Custody Projects for teenagers and this led me into Education Social Work with the Inner London Education Authority - working with a mix primary schools, secondary schools and alternative provision.
Following the birth of our first son, we moved from London to Wiltshire in 1989. I started working in the Post 16 college sector in Hampshire - where I then spent 30+ years working as a college teacher, head of department and senior manager (mainly focusing on SEND students and managing this aspect of the college curriculum.) I am now semi retired and apart from ongoing professional interests (both as a school governor and college assessor), I am a passionate football player (still playing aged 63 years old - albeit more slowly),an aspiring rock guitarist - who knows when my big break might come - and an avid supporter of the natural world and the importance it plays in our well being. I am married to an amazing person and have 4 grown up sons and 2 grandchildren.
I hope my extensive experience of working in many educational settings - along with my passion for inclusion - will be of value to the school community at Manor Fields.
I’m Bea Seggari, I became a finance governor at Manor Fields School in October 2023.I am a Chartered Accountant (CIPFA), currently working for Dorset & Wiltshire Fire Service as a Management Accountant.
Previously I worked for Wiltshire Council as a School Support Accountant and I had the pleasure to work with Manor Fields School for ten years. During this time, I followed with great interest the school’s achievements and aspirations to provide every child with the best opportunities for learning. I had a great relationship with the Senior Leadership Team. When I was asked, if I would be interested to become a governor, I jumped at the opportunity.
I hope that my extensive knowledge and experience about schools’ funding, financial reporting and regulations can benefit the school.
In my free time I enjoy traveling and discovering new countries and cultures. I like to spend time with my family and go for walks or bike rides in the New Forest.
I began my career in Land Access and Resettlement Planning for major mining and infrastructure projects across the continent of Africa, which took me to many interesting places and experienced diverse cultures. Wherever I am, I avail myself to the service of my community so there was no hesitation when I was asked to join the amazing school community as a co-opted governor having moved from London to Salisbury a year before. I currently work in programme and project management, and I look forward to working with the school and community towards the well-being of the children.
My name is Sandra Johnson, and I joined the governing body at Manor Fields Primary School with a strong commitment to supporting children’s education and wellbeing. I am a mother of four adult children and a grandmother of eight, which has given me a deep, personal understanding of the vital role schools play in shaping young lives. Alongside this, I have worked in education for over 40 years as a Teaching Assistant and Higher Level Teaching Assistant and am currently employed in this role at a local school.
I have previously served as a school governor, which has given me valuable experience and insight into the role of governance within a school setting. Through this role, I developed an understanding of the importance of supporting and challenging school leadership, working collaboratively with other governors, and keeping pupils’ best interests at the centre of decision‑making.

Manor Fields Primary School
Manor Fields Primary School
🪶 Welcome to Woodpeckers Class!
Welcome to Woodpeckers class! We have lots of exciting learning planned this term, and we are looking forward to sharing some of the wonderful learning the children have been working on.
Here is an overview of what we are getting up to across the curriculum.
As Mathematicians – Place Value
In Maths, we are learning all about place value. We have been developing our understanding of tens and ones and learning how the position of a digit affects its value.
We use Base 10 equipment to help us recognise and represent numbers up to 100. The children will have lots of opportunities to build numbers using tens and ones and explain what each digit represents.
We will be continuing to use these strategies to support in adding and subtracting two digit numbers as the term continues.
As Authors – Retelling a Narrative
In English, we will be developing our storytelling and writing skills by retelling our class story, The Goose and the Golden Egg, in our own words.
We will begin by learning how to create a story framework to help us plan the important events and structure of our story. We will then explore how writers use interesting vocabulary to make their writing more exciting.
The children will create their own expanded noun phrases to describe characters, settings and objects, which they will then use in their own retellings.
We are looking forward to seeing the children use their imaginations and writing skills to create their own versions of this traditional tale!
As Scientists – What Is Alive?
In Science, we have been exploring the question:
We have been learning about what all living things have in common and have used the acronym MRS GREN to help us remember the seven life processes:
Using MRS GREN, we have been investigating whether something is alive, dead, or has never been alive.
We have also explored the similarities and differences between different living things, including where they live and what they eat. The children have enjoyed thinking like scientists and using their observations to help answer questions about the world around them.
As Historians – The Great Fire of London
In History, we have travelled back in time to 1666 to learn about the Great Fire of London.
We have created timelines to show how the fire started and spread across London, helping us to understand the sequence of events.
We have also explored the famous diary of Samuel Pepys and used his experiences as inspiration to write our own diary entries. The children have been thinking carefully about what it might have been like to experience such a significant historical event.
As Geographers – Our Local Area
In Geography, we have been learning about the difference between human and physical features.
We have particularly focused on our local area around Salisbury and have been learning to identify the different features that can be found around us.
The children have been out and about around our school, recording data about the human and physical features they can spot.
We will use our findings to create a class display, showcasing the different features we have discovered in our local area.
Home Learning
Each Friday, the children will bring home a new set of spellings and a Maths fluency task.
These should be completed by the following Thursday, when the children's home-learning books will be collected and marked.
Termly Project
Each term, the children will also have a slightly longer home-learning project to complete.
This term, our project is to create a human and physical features poster. The children will have the whole term to work on their posters, giving them plenty of time to research, design and create something they are proud of.
We are excited to see the children's ideas and creativity!
Reading at Home
Please support your child by reading with them at least three times each week.
We ask that you record each reading session in your child's reading record. This is important as it allows your child to be entered into our reading raffle!
Reading books and reading records will be checked and renewed each Friday. Please ensure that both are returned to school alongside the home-learning books.
Thank you for your continued support with reading at home. Regular reading makes a huge difference to children's confidence, vocabulary and overall progress.
Thank You, Woodpecker Families!
We hope this gives you a helpful insight into what the children will be learning this term.
There is lots to look forward to, and we can't wait to see the children continue to learn, explore, create and grow throughout the term!
Thank you for your continued support with your child's learning at home.

Manor Fields Primary School
Manor Fields Primary School
Parents and Carers
It takes a village to raise a child
At Manor Fields, we believe children flourish when the people around them work together. Families, staff and our wider community each have something valuable to offer in helping children learn in a safe, healthy and supportive environment.
You know your child best. Your understanding of their strengths, interests and experiences helps us provide the support and encouragement they need. Together, we can help children feel secure, aim high and make the most of the opportunities school life brings.
Our partnership grows through open communication, collaboration and a shared determination to do the best for every child. By listening to one another, celebrating successes and working through challenges together, we can respond to children’s needs and help them achieve their potential.
“Alone we can do so little; together we can do so much.”— Helen Keller
How you can make a difference
There are many ways to support your child and contribute to our school community:
Support learning at home. Enjoy reading together, practise the home learning your child’s teacher recommends and take an interest in what your child is discovering. Little moments of encouragement make a difference.
Encourage participation. Help your child take a full part in school life, try new activities and discover their interests through clubs, trips and special events.
Help your child arrive ready to learn. Support regular attendance, punctuality and routines that help them feel rested and prepared for the day.
Work with us on our expectations and policies. Reinforce our school values and behaviour expectations, and speak with us if you have questions or need support.
Attend parent consultations. These conversations help us share progress, celebrate achievements and agree the next steps in your child’s learning.
Keep communication open. Let us know about changes or concerns that may affect your child. Sharing information early helps us respond with understanding and care.
Offer constructive feedback. Tell us what is working well and where we could improve. Your ideas and experiences help us strengthen our school.
Volunteer your time. Listening to children read, helping on school trips or supporting events are valuable ways to get involved. Please contact the office to explore opportunities.
Join our HSA. Help bring families together, support events and raise funds for opportunities that enrich children’s school experience.
Share your expertise. Your work, hobbies, cultural knowledge or practical skills could inspire children and bring their learning to life.
Consider becoming a school governor. When vacancies arise, this offers an opportunity to contribute to the school’s direction and development.
Every contribution matters
Whether you can offer a few minutes, an occasional helping hand or a regular commitment, we value your involvement. You do not need to volunteer or attend every event to be an important part of Manor Fields.
If you would like to get involved—or need help supporting your child—please speak to their class teacher or contact the school office. You belong in our school community, and we look forward to working with you.
